obtained.how: copy posted openly by REABIC (Regional Euro-Asian Biological Invasions Centre) in its publications folder: a re-typeset text with the original figures and tables as images (the reference list is not included)

bibliography.checked_against: Crossref and the copy's first page
bibliography.note: J. Great Lakes Res. 20(3): 537–545, 1994; Lin Wu and David A. Culver. Matches.

claims.claim: in western Lake Erie edible algae below about 4 g/m³ fresh weight suppressed Daphnia births and began the midsummer decline
claims.source_value: edible phytoplankton < 4 g m⁻³ wet weight suppressed birth rates (< 1 d⁻¹) and, with rising young-of-year yellow perch consumption, caused the midsummer decline; low edible algae 'thus initiated the midsummer decline'
claims.location: p. 1 (PDF p. 1), Abstract; pp. 8–9 (PDF pp. 8–9), Discussion; Fig. 4 (PDF p. 6)
claims.quote: birth rates (<1 individual d-1) by low edible phytoplankton resources (<4 g·m-3 wet wt)
claims.conditions: western basin of Lake Erie (eutrophic, > 50 µg/L TP), June–August 1989, nearshore (6 m) and offshore (10 m) pooled; biomass from biovolume at specific gravity 1; D. galeata mendotae and D. retrocurva
claims.note: The authors pair the food limit with predation: the decline began when low food suppressed births and young perch consumption rose.

claims.claim: in western Lake Erie young yellow perch accounted for all D. galeata mendotae mortality from 4 to 11 July
claims.source_value: a bioenergetics estimate: young-of-year yellow perch alone accounted for the total D. g. mendotae mortality between 4 and 11 July, at the start of the decline; over the decline as a whole, 50 %
claims.location: p. 9 (PDF p. 9), Discussion; p. 7 (PDF p. 7), Results; Fig. 5 (PDF p. 8)
claims.quote: YOY yellow perch alone accounted for the total D. g. mendotae mortality
claims.conditions: 1989; consumption from a yellow perch bioenergetics model (Hewett & Johnson 1992, adjusted after Post 1990) using trawl densities (25-mm cod end), diet by dry weight, mean depth 8 m
claims.note: The rewrite could add 'by a bioenergetics estimate' and that over the whole decline the share was 50 % (p. 7).

notes: Other values: young perch fed only on copepods in early June and selected D. g. mendotae from 6 July (> 30 mm TL; Table 2); D. retrocurva was rarely eaten yet declined the same way, earlier; the egg development time used is D = 1/(0.00041T² + 0.0108T − 0.0163) d (Luecke et al. 1990). Extrapolating the perch model to all young-of-year fish (mostly white perch) gave far more than 100 % of mortality, which the authors judge unreasonable.
